source_text: Priori ergo operi quattuor libellis ea, quam suppeditavit veritas, facultate respondi; praefatus sane praeteriturum me, quae et pro dogmate illius nihil habere ponderis apparebat, et me possent arguere multiloquii, si fuissem imbecilla quaeque et inania persecutus. Quamquam, si hanc regulam, ut decuit, servare licuisset, id est ut nec oppugnationem ex professione inepta mererentur, pene omnia eius inventa publico fuerant spernenda silentio. Sed quoniam, rebus in peiorem partem properantibus (quod mundi fini suo incumbentis indicium est), in Ecclesia quoque Dei adepta est stultitia et turpitudo dominatum; pro Christo legatione fungimur [n11] , et pro virili portione quantum valemus opis, ad defensionem catholicae religionis afferimus; nec piget mandare litteris remedia, quae contra errorum venena conficimus.
pass_a_gloss: To the earlier work therefore I answered in four little books with that ability which truth supplied; having first said that I would pass by things which both were appearing to have no weight for his dogma, and could charge me with much-speaking, if I had pursued every weak and empty thing. And yet, if it had been allowed to keep this rule as was fitting, that is that they should not even deserve an attack as professionally inept, almost all his inventions would have had to be scorned by public silence. But since, with things hurrying into the worse part (which is a sign of a world leaning on its own end), folly and turpitude have obtained mastery even in the Church of God; we discharge an embassy for Christ, and according to each man's portion, as much help as we can, we bring to the defense of the catholic religion; nor does it irk to commit to letters the remedies which we mix against the poisons of errors.

lemmas.lexica: LS facultas; Blaise ability to choose

pass_b_english: I therefore answered that earlier work in four little books, with whatever ability truth supplied. I stated at the outset that I would pass over things which plainly carried no weight in support of his doctrine and which might expose me to a charge of verbosity if I pursued every weak and empty remark. Indeed, if I had been permitted to keep that rule as I should, so that admitted absurdities did not even deserve an attack, almost all his inventions would have deserved the contempt of universal silence. But things are rushing toward the worse, a sign that the world is approaching its end; folly and depravity have gained power even in God's Church. We therefore serve as ambassadors for Christ (2 Corinthians 5:20), bringing such help as we can, each according to his ability, to the defense of the catholic religion. Nor are we reluctant to commit to writing the remedies we prepare against the poisons of error.

choices.why: Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
Capacity of choosing; infants lack it because they lack reason.
